What the workflow does:
- **Triggers:** it runs on tag `v*` and on `workflow_dispatch`.
- **Build job:** it builds `pkm` for the four targets. Both macOS targets build on `macos-latest`, so `x86_64-apple-darwin` is cross-compiled.
- **Artifacts:** each target uploads artifact `pkm-&lt;target&gt;` containing `pkm-&lt;target&gt;[.exe]` and a `.sha256` file with a relative filename, so `sha256sum -c` works.
- **Release job:** it runs only on tags, needs only `GITHUB_TOKEN`, re-checks the hashes, then runs `gh release create --generate-notes`. `workflow_dispatch` never creates a Release.
- **Action versions:** checkout@v7, upload-artifact@v7, download-artifact@v8 and rust-cache@v2. I chose them from `gh api` latest releases, so `ci.yml` stays on checkout@v5 and the two workflows now differ.

```
gh workflow run release.yml --ref main

gh run watch RUN_ID --exit-status
mkdir -p /tmp/rel &amp;&amp; gh run download RUN_ID --dir /tmp/rel
cd /tmp/rel &amp;&amp; for d in pkm-*/; do (cd "$d" &amp;&amp; sha256sum -c ./*.sha256); done
```
Expect four `pkm-&lt;target&gt;` directories, every checksum `OK`, and no Release created.

<result>The `platform` module is in and committed. `cargo test -p pkm-core platform` passes 15 tests on Linux, and workspace `cargo fmt --check`, `cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets -- -D warnings` and `cargo test --workspace` all pass. Nothing has run on Windows or macOS yet. I compiled and linted against both targets with clippy and both were clean, so the tests written only for those platforms will first run in CI.

**What the module does** (`crates/pkm-core/src/platform.rs`):
- **Per-user folder:** `pkm_dir()` and `cache_dir(name)` give `%LOCALAPPDATA%\pkm` (or `~\AppData\Local\pkm` if that variable is empty), `~/Library/Application Support/pkm`, and `$XDG_CACHE_HOME/pkm` or `~/.cache/pkm` on Linux. If there is no home folder it returns an error instead of guessing.
- **Name clash check:** `name_taken(dst, src)` finds an existing file whose name matches ignoring case and NFC/NFD. A case-only rename of the file itself is allowed, as in Python.
- **Safe move:** `move_file` and `move_file_with` never overwrite. If the name is taken they fail with `AlreadyExists` and the same message as Python. If another program holds the file they retry up to a limit (default 5 tries, 200 ms steps). On Windows this also covers the "file in use" error codes 32 and 33.
- **Windows rename:** Rust's own `std::fs::rename` overwrites the target on Windows, but Python's `os.rename` does not. So on Windows the module calls the system `MoveFileExW` directly, with no replace flag and with long-path support.

**Dependencies added:** `caseless` (matches Python's `casefold`), `unicode-normalization`, `windows-sys` (Windows only) and `tempfile` (tests only). `Cargo.lock` is updated.

**The 19-test table in `spec/PORTING.md`:**
- **Ported (5):** the cache-folder test and four of the `Move` tests. A few extra Rust-only tests sit alongside them.
- **Not applicable (12):** six WSL-only tests, the two `local_path` tests (that function on …[+2829]

<result>I've built two small Rust MCP servers and Claude Code called the tool on both. Q4 is decided in favour of a hand-written JSON-RPC server rather than `rmcp`. The phase stays `in-progress` until you run the Claude Desktop test on Windows.

**Claude Code test:** I ran Claude Code 2.1.316 headless with a temporary MCP config, so your global config is untouched. It completed the handshake and a tool call against both servers and returned the correct Vietnamese note ids. The full transcript is in section 5 of the report.

**Protocol version:** Python echoes the version the client asks for if it knows it (`2025-06-18`, `2025-03-26` or `2024-11-05`), otherwise it answers `2025-06-18`. Both Rust servers do exactly the same. Claude Code asked for `2025-11-25` and all three servers answered `2025-06-18`.

**One thing you should know:** Claude Code 2.1.316 first tries `server/discover` from the newer 2026-07-28 protocol. When that fails it falls back to `initialize`, and that fallback is the path Python uses. If a later Claude Code drops the fallback, the Python server breaks first. I wrote that down as the trigger for revisiting Q4.

**Why hand-written (Q4):**

| | Hand-written (`s2-hand`) | `rmcp` 3.8.0 (`s2-rmcp`) |
|---|---|---|
| Binary size (stripped release) | 0.68 MB | 2.79 MB |
| Crates pulled in | 12 | 56 |
| Clean release build | 2.5 s | 16.5 s |
| Async runtime | none | `tokio` required (it panics at runtime if timers are off) |

- **Wording control is not the deciding factor.** Both servers produce a `find` entry in `tools/list` that matches Python's string for string, key order included. A test checks this against a JSON file exported from the pinned Python code.
- **The real problem with `rmcp` is the protocol layer.** It differs from Python in five places:
  - unknown method: the error message reads `nope/x` instead of `method not found: nope/x`;
  - a line that is not JSON: no reply at all, where Pyth …[+2475]

### Results
Count of notes the index would see differently from Python (different props, different YAML error text, or one side stops):

| Candidate | kg-solo (746) | 58 edge cases | 25,000 random notes |
|---|---|---|---|
| `unsafe-libyaml` + layer | 0 | 0 | 0 |
| `libyaml-safer` + layer | 0 | 1 | 242 (all panics) |
| `saphyr-parser` + layer | 0 | 9 | 6,510 |
| `serde_norway`, used directly | 0 | 35 | 20,916 |
| `saphyr`, used directly | 0 | 36 | 21,317 |

- **kg-solo cannot tell the crates apart.** It only has strings, plain integers and lists; dates stay strings on both sides. The decision therefore rests on the edge cases and the random notes.
- **`libyaml-safer` panics** when a `|` or `&gt;` block is the last frontmatter value. That is a common shape in real notes (e.g. `description: &gt;` at the end). The bug is already reported upstream (issues #6 and #7, both open).
- **`unsafe-libyaml` is archived**, but it is the same libyaml 0.2.5 that PyYAML uses. If `libyaml-safer` fixes those two issues and the probe shows 0, switching to it removes the `unsafe` code.
- The report covers the mismatch kinds with counts and handling, and gives the layer design phase 08 should follow.

**High**
1. **H1. The stderr reader stops on bad UTF-8 and OHS then freezes** (`crates/pkm-core/src/ohs/process.rs:113-122`).
   - **Scenario:** Node, onnxruntime or another native library writes a line in the system code page (for example CP1258). `lines()` returns `Err(InvalidData)` and the reader thread exits, so nothing reads stderr any more. The pipe fills up (about 4 KB on Windows, 64 KB on Linux) and every `console.error` in OHS blocks. Its event loop stops.
   - **Effect:** stdout stays open, so no `Exited` event is sent and there is never a restart or a `broken` state. Every search times out after 60 s, and `state()` keeps reporting `starting`.
   - **Fix:** read with `read_until(b'\n')` plus `from_utf8_lossy`, and always keep reading until EOF. Add a fake-server test that writes a `0xFF` byte to stderr followed by more than 64 KB.
2. **H2. The stdin write holds a mutex with no time limit, and `close()` needs that same mutex** (`process.rs:191-194`, `process.rs:236`, `crates/pkm-core/src/ohs.rs:354-361`).
   - **Scenario:** OHS is alive but has stopped reading stdin (H1 causes this). The pipe fills and one caller blocks in `write_all` while holding the lock.
   - **Effect:** the other callers block on the lock, and `request_timeout` does not apply because it only covers waiting for the reply. The supervisor blocks too, in `observe` or in `close()`. `Drop for Ohs` waits for the supervisor with no limit, so `pkm` never exits.
   - **Fix:** `close()` should use `try_lock` on stdin and fall back to killing the child after the timeout; the kil …[+4408]

<summary>Agent "Phase 11a OHS module" finished</summary>
<note>A task-notification fires each time this agent stops with no live background children of its own. The user can send it another message and resume it, so the same task-id may notify more than once.</note>
<result>All the review findings you listed are fixed in one new commit, `2c8b25a14bcb7511670aaf22fb01859aa9dc4592`, on branch `worktree-agent-a94d3311e16f541ad`, on top of `d257923`. Nothing was pushed or merged. The Windows and macOS code passes clippy for those targets, but the tests have only run on Linux so far; CI will be the first run there.

**What changed:**
- **H1, M1 (readers):** stdout and stderr are read to EOF, line by line, with invalid UTF-8 replaced instead of stopping the reader. A stdout line that can't be parsed is ignored as noise.
- **H2 (stdin writes):** a dedicated writer thread now owns stdin and takes lines from a channel, so `call` never blocks past its timeout. `close()` just drops the channel sender, so it never waits on a lock a stuck writer holds; if OHS doesn't exit in time it is killed, which unblocks the writer.
- **M2 (dead process, child processes):**
  - The supervisor checks `try_wait` every `poll_interval`, including while waiting for `ready`.
  - On Unix, OHS runs in its own process group. The whole group is killed before reaping, and swept once right after reaping (POSIX does not reuse a PID while a group with that ID still exists). This uses the new `libc` dependency.
  - On Windows, OHS runs in a Job Object with kill-on-close and is stopped with `TerminateJobObject`. If the job can't be created or assigned, only node is killed. This needed new windows-sys features.
- **M3 (cached state):** the supervisor asks for `status` right after `ready` and then every `poll_interval`, and caches the result. `search` and `state()` reuse it if it is less than two intervals old. A `status` timeout keeps the previous state instead of reporting `starting`.
- **M4 (status errors):** only three rejected or malformed `status` replies in a row make the state `broken`. It goes back to `ready` once OHS answers correctly again.
- **L1:** reader and writer threads use `thread::Builder`; if one c …[+2773]

<result>I found no SQL injection and no panics in this diff. The main real defect is a build that fails partway through and leaves the index wrong for good. The Python spec has the same flaw, so the parity tests can't catch it. `cargo test -p pkm-core` exited without errors, but I only saw the last lines (the doctest run with 0 tests), so I haven't confirmed the unit tests themselves passed. The full report, in Vietnamese, is at `/home/vantt/projects/obsidian-pkm/plans/reports/code-reviewer-261102-1500-index.md`.

**High**

1. **A failed build leaves links and edges stale until someone runs `--full`.** (`crates/pkm-core/src/index.rs:655-679`, `693-707`, `781-791`)
   - **What happens:** note rows, including the new mtime and size, are saved in the first transaction. Edges and views are saved in a second one, and meta in a third.
   - **Failure scenario:** if `derive` fails after the first transaction is saved, the next incremental build sees no changed notes. That can happen if the adapter returns an error (e.g. a bad `data.score` at `adapter/e11.rs:603`), the schema fails to load, or the process is killed. The schema digest in meta still matches, so it skips recomputing edges. Old links and edges then stay in place, and no note ever looks "changed" again to trigger a fix.
   - **Same in Python:** `index.py:186` and `:215` use two separate `with db` blocks.
   - **Fix:** write a `meta.dirty=1` flag before the first transaction, clear it in the meta transaction, and force `derive` while it is set. Alternatively, merge the first two transactions. Either way, a successful build produces the same rows and `edges.id` values.

2. **The write lock is held while files are read, and lock conflicts aren't handled.** (`index.rs:656-678`, `618`)
   - **What happens:** `write_note` reads and parses each file inside the write transaction. On a large vault or a synced or network drive on Windows, the lock lasts second …[+3667]

The first installable Windows release has three blockers: the Windows binary may not start on a clean machine, there is no installer, and there are no user install steps.

The audit covers `main` at `7d14601` and was read-only. I could not run the binary-based checks: the repo's `scout-block` hook blocks both `cargo build` and the `target/` folder. So those results come from reading the source, not from running `pkm`. The project fits the skill's "single binary" model, and mdview is the closest reference project. Those questions are about the OHS artifact pinning, the command names (`mcp install` versus the skill's `init`/`update`/`uninstall`), and Linux using `-gnu` rather than `-musl`. None of them asks to change a decision.

Top 5 findings:
- **Blocker, the Windows binary needs `vcruntime140.dll`** (`release.yml:91`, no `crt-static` setting anywhere). Many clean Windows machines don't have that DLL, so Claude Desktop would fail to start `pkm.exe`. Fix: build with `crt-static` and add a CI check that the DLL dependency is gone.
- **Blocker, no installer or stable install location.** The release ships a bare `.exe` (`release.yml:100`), and `mcp install` records wherever that file happens to be (`install.rs:182`), for example the Downloads folder. Fix: an `install.ps1` that verifies the hash, installs to `%LOCALAPPDATA%\pkm\bin`, and also handles update and uninstall. Also make `mcp install` warn when it is run from outside that folder.
- **Blocker, no quick start for users.** `README …[+1576]

<note>A task-notification fires each time this agent stops with no live background children of its own. The user can send it another message and resume it, so the same task-id may notify more than once.</note>
<result>I fixed all seven review findings in commit `53c1156fd0dcc062602838318775bceb26e8b4ff` on `worktree-agent-ad762b84a2a65e3be`. I merged main first (a fast-forward to 7d14601) and did not push or merge.

Successful builds are still byte-identical to Python. I re-compared whole databases after full, no-change, edited-incremental, second incremental and full-rebuild steps. That covered kg-solo, the planted-error vault from `test_kg.py` and the e11 vault from `test_kg_adapter.py`. The CI-style parity check on kg-solo shows 0 unnamed diffs, exit 0.

1. **Failed build leaves edges stale (high):** the note-table transaction now also writes a `dirty` row in `meta`, which only goes away when the final `meta` is written. If that row is still there on the next build, edges are re-derived. `failed_build_is_rederived_next_time` injects an adapter failure to check this.
2. **Concurrent builds (high):**
   - Notes are now read and parsed before the write transaction opens.
   - All write transactions are `IMMEDIATE`, with an explicit 30 s busy timeout.
   - A lock file `&lt;db&gt;.lock` sits next to the DB, so only one build writes at a time. A second build waits up to 5 minutes, then fails with an error. Python has no such lock, so this is recorded as an intended deviation.
   - If the filesystem doesn't support file locks (some network drives), the build runs unlocked, as Python does.
   - Because builds are serialized, the previous file list and `meta` are read under the lock rather than inside a transaction.
   - `concurrent_builds_take_turns` covers this.
3. **WAL mode (medium):** the build only switches to WAL if the DB isn't already in WAL, and doesn't wait for a lock when switching. If the switch fails, it keeps the old mode and carries on (`wal_switch_failure_is_not_fatal`).
4. **mtime+size detection (medium):** the limits (FAT/exFAT, sync tools keeping the original mtime) and `--full` as the fix are …[+1534]

**1. Đang sửa (agent đang chạy, xong là merge):**
- **Lỗi chặn 1:** build `pkm.exe` với CRT tĩnh để không cần `vcruntime140.dll`. Kèm một bước CI fail nếu binary còn phụ thuộc DLL đó.

- **Workflow release:** chạy test trước khi phát hành, kiểm tag khớp phiên bản crate, gộp một file `checksums.txt`, chạy thử `pkm --version` cho từng binary, đánh dấu tag có `-rc` là prerelease. CI cũng build bản release trên mỗi lần push, để lỗi đóng gói lộ sớm thay vì đợi lúc gắn tag.

**2. Tôi làm ngay sau khi phase 12 merge (đụng `crates/pkm`, đang có agent khác sửa):**

<result>## Phase Implementation Report

All three blockers and the release-pipeline items are fixed, including the private-repo change: the installers try the public URL first and fall back to `gh` on 401/403/404. The Windows installer (`install.ps1`) has never been run, because the worktree hook blocks `pwsh` here. Its first real run will be on the Windows CI runner.

- **Branch:** `worktree-agent-a1f9526676784076c`, HEAD `4cc7dbd7be74daa2456a6f5f4d8dd97cdf94c989`, five commits on top of `7d14601`. Nothing pushed, merged or tagged.

### What changed
- **Blocker 1, no `vcruntime140.dll`:** `.cargo/config.toml` builds the Windows binary with a static CRT. On every packaging run, `scripts/release-assets.sh` lists the DLLs `pkm.exe` imports with `dumpbin` and fails if any C runtime DLL is still there.
- **Blocker 2, install scripts:** `scripts/install.ps1` and `scripts/install.sh` do the following:
  - Check sha256 against one combined `checksums.txt` and run `pkm --version` before replacing anything.
  - Install to `%LOCALAPPDATA%\pkm\bin` or `~/.local/bin` and add it to the user PATH. Uninstall removes exactly what was added.
  - Update when re-run; the same version does nothing. On Windows, a `pkm.exe` that Claude Desktop is running gets renamed out of the way.
  - Offer `--uninstall`, `--dry-run`, and `--mcp-install &lt;vault&gt;` (only runs `pkm mcp install` when passed).
  - Let you change the source repo or URL with `PKM_RELEASE_REPO` / `-Repo` and `PKM_RELEASE_BASE_URL` / `-ReleaseBaseUrl`.
  - Stay ASCII-only. Windows PowerShell 5.1 garbles Vietnamese diacritics when it reads a script through `irm`, so installer messages are in English.
- **Blocker 3, README:** Vietnamese quick start using `gh auth login`, the `gh release download … | Out-String | iex` one-liner, `pkm mcp install`, `pkm doctor`, update/uninstall, and the SmartScreen workaround. The status line now says no release exists yet.

<result>I've fixed all three causes of the red CI and committed them on `main`, but nothing is pushed. Please push `cc8af51`, `c7bf21e` and `2f83462` (they sit on top of `0054429`) so CI runs again. The Windows fix has not run on a Windows machine yet.

**1. Parity step failing on all 3 OS (since run 41408080051).**
- **Cause:** `Swatinem/rust-cache` saves `target/` but deletes every file outside cargo's build folders, and keeps the empty folders. Run 41406769089 (commit `8f64929`) was the first time the Rust dump wrote subfolders (`tables/`, `cli/`, `mcp/`). That run saved a cache in which `target/parity/rust-dump` held only those empty folders and no `manifest.json`.
- **Why everything after that failed:** from the next run (41408080051) on, the cache was restored as an exact match, so the check found a non-empty dump folder with no manifest and refused to overwrite it. The `2661aa0` commit doesn't touch `parity/`; it was just the first run to use the bad cache. Locally the check passes because nothing ever cleans your `target/`.
- **Proof:** I created those empty folders and ran `check --dump-out` on them locally. It gives exactly the CI message and exit code 2.
- **Fix (`cc8af51`):** `ci.yml` now passes `--dump-out "$RUNNER_TEMP/rust-dump"`, so the dump is written outside the cache. The check's "don't delete a folder that isn't a dump" safeguard stays as it was.

**2. Windows: `mcp::tests::handshake` and `tools_list_comes_from_the_tool_layer`.**
- **Cause:** a real product bug, not a test problem. `instructions::basename` only split paths on `/`, so on Windows the vault name became the whole path (`C:\Users\...\Vault thử`). That wrong name went into the MCP instructions and the `obsidian://` link.
- **Python reference:** the Python spec (`mcp_server.py:89,93,200`) uses `ntpath.basename`, which splits on both `\` and `/` and drops the drive letter. I checked its behaviour on several Windows paths.

- **B2, binary location:** `pkm mcp install` now refuses without `--force` when the running `pkm` is outside a stable install location. A stable location is one of:
  - the standard folder, set by one constant, `STANDARD_BIN_DIR`: `%LOCALAPPDATA%\pkm\bin` on Windows, `~/.local/bin` elsewhere;
  - the folder in `PKM_INSTALL_DIR`;
  - a folder holding the installer's `.pkm-managed` marker.

  These match the defaults in the `install.ps1`/`install.sh` being written in the other worktree. The refusal says when the file is in Downloads or a temp folder. It prints the installer command (via `gh release download`, since the repo is private) and the command to re-run from the standard folder with the same vault and flags. `--dry-run` only shows the warning.
- **I2, missing OHS:** this is now a `warn` that says only `related` without `hits` is affected. Installing with `--no-ohs` writes `"env": {"PKM_NO_OHS": "1"}` into the `kg` entry, and doctor then shows `skip`. A later install without `--no-ohs` removes it.
- **I3, read-only doctor:** by default doctor only checks the package files and `node --version`, as a new check `ohs_node`. It starts OHS only with `--deep`, which replaces `--no-ohs-start`. Every OHS problem is at most a `warn`.
- **I4, JSON output:** `doctor --json` prints `{schema:1, ok, data:{checks:[{id,status,detail,action,fix}]}, error, next}`.
  - `fix` is either a re-install or a rebuild of the index. It is built from the `kg` entry's own arguments and quoted for PowerShell on Windows or `sh` …[+2953]

**How it matches Python exactly:**
- **Summing:** the Python that built the golden (3.14) sums floats with error compensation, so `related::py_sum` copies CPython's algorithm. A plain sum is off in the last bit.
- **Edge order:** edges are read with Python's exact SQL, which has no `ORDER BY`.
- **Queue and ordering:** the push queue, the order nodes first get mass, and all sorts behave like Python's `deque`, `dict` and stable sort.
- **Rounding:** `round(x, 5)` rounds ties to even, as in Python.
- **Bad arguments:** where Python raises, Rust returns an error with the same exception name.

<result>I found two high-severity bugs that can hang the MCP server, plus several medium and low issues. Nothing on the main path corrupts the Claude Desktop config, and stdout carries only JSON-RPC. This was a read-only review: I didn't run the code, the tests or a repro. The full report (in Vietnamese) is at `/home/vantt/projects/obsidian-pkm/plans/reports/code-reviewer-261102-1550-pkm-crate.md`.

## High

**H1. A panic during the first index build makes every `tools/call` hang forever.** `crates/pkm/src/mcp.rs:258-271` and `:331`
- **Failure:** `first_build` only calls `set_ready()` after the build returns. If `index::build`, `adapter::load` or `open_tools` panics (say, on a malformed note), the background thread dies and the ready flag is never set.
- **Effect:** `initialize` and `tools/list` give up after their 20 s wait and carry on. But `tools/call` uses `wait_ready(None)`, which has no limit. The tool never answers and the server never exits, so Claude Desktop shows no error.
- **Fix:** wrap the body of `first_build` in `catch_unwind`, or use a guard whose `Drop` calls `set_ready`. Give `tools/call` a timeout and return `{"error":"index unavailable"}` when it expires.

**H2. `paths`, `loops` and `all_loops` have no limit, so one tool call can lock the server indefinitely.** `crates/pkm-core/src/query.rs:744-792`, `:796`, `:861`
- **Failure:** the recursive SQL query lists every simple path up to `max_len` edges. `max_len` comes straight from the model with no ceiling. There is no row limit and no way to interrupt the query.
- **Effect:** on a vault with a few thousand densely linked notes, `max_len` around 8–10 explodes combinatorially (CPU 100%, RAM growing until the OS kills the process). The server is single-threaded and holds the `state` lock, so every later request, including `ping`, is stuck. This behaviour was inherited from the Python version.
- **Fix:** cap `max_len` (around 6) at the tool la …[+4667]

**`928ddbf`: OHS for `related` in the MCP server and CLI**

*MCP server:*
- It starts one OHS in the background at startup, so `initialize` answers immediately.
- While OHS is still starting, `related` with only `query` returns `ohs_not_ready` with `state: starting`.
- The OHS is attached to the tool session and survives graph reopens. `Server::shutdown()` stops it when stdin closes.

*Package lookup:* `--ohs &lt;dir&gt;` first, then `PKM_OHS_DIR`, then the package that `pkm mcp install` installed. `PKM_NO_OHS=1` means no OHS.

*Old Python flags (my decision):*
- `--ohs-cli` / `KG_OHS_CLI`: used only if it points at an OHS package (the package dir, or `&lt;pkg&gt;/app/dist/src/cli.js`); otherwise warned about on stderr and ignored. A leftover Python `KG_OHS_CLI` therefore can't break the default package.
- `--ohs-node`: accepted and ignored, because the package ships its own Node.

*New CLI command `pkm VAULT related`:*
- The query is the positional words; `--hit PATH` (repeatable) gives seeds directly and needs no OHS. `--k`, `--types` and the usual filters apply.
- With only a query, it starts OHS for that one call and waits up to `--ohs-wait` seconds (default 60, matching Python's one-shot timeout), then shuts OHS down.
- If the result has an `error` (including `ohs_not_ready`), the JSON goes to stdout, `related: &lt;error&gt;` goes to stderr, and it exits 1.

<result>I've written the Windows handoff, updated the plan, and committed as `f861963` on local `main` without pushing. Because of that, the Windows agent can't get the handoff file through `gh repo clone` until you push or copy it over.

**Where the binary comes from:** there's no tag or Release yet, so the handoff tells the agent to run the Release workflow by hand (`workflow_dispatch`). It then downloads the `release-assets` artifact and runs `install.ps1 -LocalFixture &lt;dir&gt;`. If a Release appears later, the README one-liner applies instead. First it must check that CI on `main` is green and stop with BLOCKED if it isn't. That matters right now: CI for `93d1251` was still running when I checked, and the last manual Release run (on an older commit) failed.

**What the handoff covers:**
- **Order of work:** part A (install, Claude Desktop, `doctor`, OHS) runs while the machine is still clean, i.e. before any Python is installed. Part B (vault-B checks and the YAML probe) comes after, because it needs Python, Node and Rust.

<result>I ported 223c9c3 into the Rust OHS module, raised the pin to 223c9c3 and rebuilt the golden. All gates pass and parity is clean.

Branch `worktree-agent-ae8cc8b9ca4b8eb75`, two commits, not pushed or merged:
- `ae2ffa1` feat(ohs): run OHS with the bundle's Vietnamese language pack
- `8f37d6f` chore(spec): pin the Python spec at 223c9c3 and regenerate the golden

**What was ported.** The part that matters is that every OHS process gets `OHS_LANGUAGE_PACK` pointing at the bundle's `lang/ohs-lang-vi`. Without that, `pkm` and the user's MCP `ohs` would use different pack settings on the shared index, and OHS would keep rebuilding its pack views. `OhsPackage` now has a `pack` field, set when that folder exists, and `ohs::LANGUAGE_PACK_ENV` is new. Every OHS launch in `pkm` sets the variable when there is a pack and leaves the environment alone when there isn't. That covers MCP, `pkm VAULT related` and `doctor --deep`. Adding the field is additive within the workspace; only two test struct literals needed it.

**Marked not applicable** (each with its reason in the PORTING row):
- The npm-install branch of `ohs_install`: Rust only runs the fork bundle (PRD §9).
- `WSLENV`: WSL-only.
- The bundle's own node in `related` and `desktop_config`: Rust already does this, and the `kg` entry doesn't carry `--ohs-node`.
- The new `OHS_CLI` constants: Rust finds the bundle another way, and an old `--ohs-cli` pointing at `app/dist/src/cli.js` is still accepted.

There are no new deliberate deviations.

**Bundle pin unchanged.** I checked the installer's pinned artifact (run 41398112909, linux-x64, sha matches the pin). It already contains `lang/ohs-lang-vi` (vi 0.2.0), and its `bin/ohs` does not set the variable, so `pkm` has to. Running that real bundle with the variable on kg-solo, `status` reported `language_pack.loaded: true`, and the ignored `ohs_real` test passed.

|---|---|---|---|

| C: thêm tool `run` (QuickJS nhúng) | khoảng 4,8 nghìn | 1–2 | 4–6 ngày sau B |
| D: chép cơ chế của browser-worker | như B | không đổi | 1–4 ngày |

Phương án B chi tiết:
- **`search`:** chỉ phơi một nhóm tham số đã chọn, giữ đúng tên mà MCP của OHS dùng (`snippet_length`, `path`), và `pkm` tự đổi sang tên của giao thức stdio. Kết quả bỏ các mảng link và thêm `type` lấy từ index.
- **`read`:** `pkm` tự đọc file, dạng kết quả giống OHS.
- **`related`:** nhận `query`, `queries`, `path` làm đường chính, vẫn nhận `hits`. Câu D1 còn 2 lượt thay 3 và bớt khoảng 2,5 nghìn token; câu D3 cũng còn 2 lượt.

- `pkm mcp install` sẽ cho OHS index vault ngay lúc cài, có cờ để bỏ qua bước này.

**Report:** I cherry-picked `0bb85c6` onto `main` (it is now `aadcd3c`).

**Fixes (commit `04811f4`):**
- **Path masking:** `Scrub` in `parity/dump-python.py` now also masks the JSON-escaped form of each vault and DB path (backslashes doubled), longest first, the same way the Rust `Scrub::new` does. On Linux both forms are identical, so the golden does not change. I checked it with Windows-style paths simulated on Linux, and both paths were replaced by `&lt;VAULT&gt;` and `&lt;DB&gt;`. This was the cause of the two CLI diffs in phase 10.
- **Vietnamese output crash:** `parity.py`, `dump-python.py` and `pyyaml-dump.py` now switch stdout and stderr to UTF-8 at startup. With `PYTHONIOENCODING=cp1252`, a plain `print` still crashes the way it did on Windows, but all three scripts run to the end.
- **PyYAML not found:** the probe in `probes/s1-yaml/src/main.rs` now runs Python with `-E -P` instead of `-I`.
  - `-I` is `-E -s -P`, and `-s` is the part that hides the user site where `pip install --user` puts PyYAML.
  - `-E` still ignores `PYTHON*` variables, and `-P` still keeps the script directory and cwd off `sys.path`, so nothing is imported from the vault.
  - `-P` needs Python 3.11 or later, which the handoff already requires. The commit message explains this choice.

**Handoff and plan (commit `f897699`):**
- **Handoff corrections:**

**Review.** One real bug, now fixed in commit `2d000c2`. The branch replaced the package in pkm's own `ohs` directory whenever its version was *different* from the pin, so a *newer* package would have been downgraded. Your case shows it: a v0.17.2-vantt.4 package in that directory, with `main` still pinning vantt.3, would have been swapped back to vantt.3.
- I added `ohs_bundle::older_than_pin`, which compares versions of the form `X.Y.Z[-vantt.N]`. Only an older package, or one with no version, gets upgraded. A package that is equal, newer, or has a version it can't compare is kept.
- `doctor` now warns only for older packages and reports newer ones as ok. It suggests the `pkm mcp install` fix only when the package is in the default directory, since reinstalling never touches a package given with `--ohs`.
- A package given with `--ohs DIR` is never overwritten. The branch already behaved this way; there is now a test for it.

Everything else you asked me to check was correct, so I left it unchanged:
- Windows paths are made absolute and escaped correctly in the config JSON.
- Config writes still use compare-and-swap.
- `doctor` only reads.
- `language_pack.loaded=false` is reported as broken with all 5 not-ready keys.
- The `OBSIDIAN_IGNORE_PATTERNS` value is sent only when the package has `lang/ohs-lang-vi`.
- A failed download leaves the old package in place.

> The job was not started because recent account payments have failed or your spending limit needs to be increased.

Repo đang private, nên CI dùng số phút Actions tính phí của tài khoản. Có vẽ tài khoản đã hết hạn mức, hoặc lần thanh toán gần nhất bị lỗi. Không job nào được khởi động, kể cả job dựng binary. Vì vậy tôi chưa tạo tag `v0.1.0-rc.3`: tạo lúc này thì workflow phát hành cũng không chạy được.

Tôi không dựng thay trên máy này được, vì không cross-compile được binary Windows và macOS đúng như CI làm.

**Anh cần làm:** vào GitHub, mục **Settings → Billing & plans**, kiểm tra phương thức thanh toán hoặc nâng spending limit cho Actions. Xong anh báo tôi. Tôi sẽ chạy lại CI trên nhánh `phase-17-one-door` (commit `535bc55` đã có version `0.1.0-rc.3`), CI xanh thì tag, rồi kiểm sha256 của Release.

Một cách khác là chuyển repo sang public, khi đó Actions miễn phí. Nhưng anh đã quyết giữ private, nên tôi không làm việc này.

Repo đã public, nên giờ cài không cần `gh` đăng nhập nữa. Trên Windows (thay `<vault>` bằng đường dẫn vault):
```powershell

pkm doctor
```

Nếu anh đã có `gh` thì lệnh cũ vẫn chạy được: `gh release download v0.1.0-rc.3 --repo vantt/obsidian-pkm --pattern install.ps1 --output - | Out-String | iex`.

Cài xong, những thay đổi anh sẽ thấy:
- Claude Desktop chỉ còn một server MCP tên **`pkm`**, có 13 tool, trong đó có `search` và `read`.
- Lúc cài, `pkm` cho OHS index vault luôn. Thêm `--no-warm` nếu muốn bỏ bước này.
- Mục `kg` cũ do `pkm` ghi sẽ được đổi tên thành `pkm`. Mục `ohs` anh tự thêm thì giữ nguyên, nhưng `pkm doctor` sẽ cảnh báo là không còn cần.

Tôi đã ghi vào plan và `docs/DECISIONS.md` (commit `3102ccd`) hai việc: rc.3 ra từ nhánh, và repo chuyển sang public. Trước khi ghi, tôi đã rà lịch sử git theo các mẫu token và khoá, không thấy bí mật nào. Main vẫn ở rc.2. Nhánh phase 17 merge vào main sau tuần chạy song song.

Anh dùng thử tuần này và ghi lại số lượt gọi tool cùng chất lượng câu trả lời. Số đó dùng cho phần đo playbook A–D của phase 17.

**Phase 10 (2 lệch ở tầng CLI):**
- Lỗi nằm ở script so khớp của repo này: `Scrub` trong `dump-python.py` không che được đường dẫn Windows khi nó nằm trong JSON. Lỗi đã được sửa trên main.
- CI vẫn chạy so khớp trên Windows hằng ngày, nhưng chỉ với vault thử kg-solo. Hai lệch kia chỉ lộ ra trên vault thật (bản B).
- Bản B không bao giờ được đưa lên CI. Vì vậy chỉ máy có bản B mới xác nhận được bản sửa, bằng lệnh `parity.py run --private`. Ở đây chỉ còn việc chạy lại để xác nhận, không còn gì phải sửa.

**Phase 13 (cài trên máy không có Python):**
- Đây là kiểm `install.ps1` và `pkm mcp install` của repo này. Mục tiêu của bản Rust là người dùng không cần Python.
- Việc này không cần máy anh hay bản B. Tôi có thể thêm một job CI trên `windows-latest` gỡ Python khỏi `PATH`, rồi chạy `install.ps1`, `pkm mcp install` với kg-solo, và `pkm doctor`. Mỗi lần push đều được kiểm, nên mục này của phase 13 đóng lại được mà không phải nhờ ai.

Vậy việc 6 tôi nhận làm. Việc 5 chỉ còn một lệnh chạy trên máy có bản B.

Anh đồng ý thì tôi làm cùng lúc ba việc: job CI không Python (việc 6), sửa hướng dẫn cài không cần `gh` (việc 7), và xoá hai nhánh đã gộp (việc 8). Tất cả làm trên main, và tôi cũng đưa vào nhánh phase 17.

Một lượt trước đã nhặt các chuyện sau từ phiên này:
<picked>
K1. Port cả hệ thống Python sang Rust bằng 14 phase, chạy nhiều agent song song
K2. Stop hook giữ agent lại suốt nhiều lượt vì điều kiện 'xong cả plan' không đạt được
K3. Gom các câu hỏi cổng thành một lần hỏi người dùng
K4. Parity harness: số mục «chưa có» từ 47 giảm về 0 qua từng merge
K5. Thứ tự liệt kê file của hệ điều hành làm đầu ra Python đổi
K6. Thử 5 thư viện YAML: 0 lệch trên 746 note, nhưng 25.000 note sinh ngẫu nhiên lộ panic
K7. Một note 338 byte làm RAM lên 1,45 GB: bom alias YAML
K8. Reviewer agent tìm lệnh đường đi có thể làm treo server MCP
K9. OHS đứng hẳn khi stderr gặp byte UTF-8 lỗi, trên máy có code page Việt
K10. CI đỏ trên cả ba OS vì cache xoá file dump, và tên vault trên Windows bị sai
K11. Audit đóng gói nói chưa kiểm được, hoá ra đã chạy thử được bằng workflow
K12. Hook chặn thư mục build và lệnh sleep dài
K13. Repo private: artifact của Actions bắt đăng nhập, đến rc.3 đổi sang public
K14. Actions bị khoá vì thanh toán lỗi, mọi job không chạy kể cả dựng binary
K15. Rà lịch sử git tìm khoá trước khi đổi repo sang public
K16. Hai agent thiết kế MCP độc lập, phản biện chéo và sửa con số token
K17. Code mode bị loại vì Claude Desktop không có shell
K18. Khoá ohs_not_ready bị compact() xoá, test không bắt được
K19. read: pkm tự đọc file thay vì chuyển qua OHS
K20. Python thêm gói tiếng Việt: thiếu biến môi trường thì index dựng lại mãi
K21. Thư viện MCP chính thức lớn gấp 4 lần, nên tự viết JSON-RPC
K22. Rust rename ghi đè file trên Windows, Python thì không
K23. PowerShell 5.1 làm hỏng dấu tiếng Việt khi đọc script qua irm
K24. Máy Windows thử ra ba lỗi harness: đường dẫn JSON, UTF-8 khi pipe, và -I ẩn user site
K25. Kiểm downgrade: «khác phiên bản» suýt hạ cấp gói OHS đang mới hơn
K26. Phát hành rc.3 từ nhánh chưa merge, theo ý người duyệt
K27. Lỗi nằm cả ở spec Python: build lỗi giữa chừng khiến index sai mãi
K28. Cờ --force bị tách thành hai cờ riêng
K29. Gộp 7 nhánh song song vào main, PORTING.md bị lặp hai lần
K30. Chạy Claude Code headless với config MCP tạm, không đụng config thật
K31. Release rc: job macOS bị huỷ vì chờ runner 15 phút, rerun gặp HTTP 500
K32. OHS tắt khi stdin đóng, probe 6 truy vấn đồng thời khớp 6 trên 6 với CLI
</picked>

Nhiệm vụ của bạn chỉ là bước người ngoài. Người đọc: dev làm một mình, dùng AI hằng ngày, không rành lĩnh vực của phiên này.
Tìm những việc user hoặc agent làm trơn tru, coi là hiển nhiên, không ai trong phiên ngạc nhiên, nhưng người đọc kia sẽ hỏi lại "làm sao vậy?" hoặc "tôi cũng muốn có cái đó". Bỏ qua những việc mà dev bình thường đã làm (chạy test, commit, đọc log...). Với mỗi việc, so với cách làm phổ biến thật sự ngoài đời, không so với chuẩn chuyên gia.
Liệt kê 3-8 việc. Mỗi việc: what, common_practice, gap (khác ở đâu, vì sao người đọc muốn biết), lines, already_picked (id ở đầu dòng nếu trùng chuyện đã nhặt, không thì null).
Riêng tư: không ghi tên note, đường dẫn trong vault, câu hỏi thật, tên người.
Chỉ trả JSON: {"outsider":[{"what":"","common_practice":"","gap":"","lines":[],"already_picked":null}]}
